g1.label: 1. Which app is ___ (good), Duolingo or Babbel?

g2.label: 2. This jacket is ___ for a winter in Hamburg.
g2.why: Not + adjective + enough: not warm enough.

g3.label: 3. Cycling at night is ___ (dangerous) than cycling in the day.

g4.label: 4. Of all the cities I have visited, Lisbon is the ___ (beautiful).
g4.why: Superlative of a long adjective: the most beautiful.

g5.label: 5. The seminar room was ___ crowded for everyone to hear the speaker.
g5.why: Too goes before an adjective: too crowded.

g6.label: 6. I have ___ books on my desk, so I can’t find my laptop.
g6.why: Books are countable, so use too many.

g7.label: 7. The exam was not as ___ (hard) as I feared.
g7.why: In not as … as the adjective keeps its basic form.

g8.label: 8. Studying at home is much ___ (cheap) than renting a study room.

g9.label: 9. Is the café quiet ___ to work in?
g9.why: Enough follows an adjective: quiet enough.

g10.label: 10. There isn’t ___ space in my room for a second desk.
g10.why: Enough comes before a noun: enough space.

g11.label: 11. At eight o’clock last night I ___ (cook) when my flatmate came home.
g11.why: The cooking was in progress when the flatmate arrived: past continuous.

g12.label: 12. I would be grateful ___ you could confirm the date.
g12.why: I would be grateful if you could… is a polite request.
